companies.name: TSMC (Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company)
companies.role: Contract foundry that manufactures the world's most advanced logic chips for companies that only design them
companies.description: TSMC invented the pure-play foundry model in 1987: it designs nothing itself, it just builds other people's chips — Nvidia's Blackwell, Apple's A- and M-series, AMD's Instinct, Broadcom's custom accelerators — often on the same campus, for direct competitors. It is responsible for north of 90% of the world's leading-edge logic production, which is why a strait 130 km wide has become the single biggest tail risk in the global economy. Under US pressure it has opened Fab 21 in Arizona (N4 volume production from Q4 2024) and JASM in Kumamoto (12/16nm and 22/28nm from December 2024), but the company openly concedes its overseas sites run a node generation or two behind: the newest process is still made almost exclusively in Hsinchu and Tainan. The gap is not equipment — everyone can buy from the Big Five — it is decades of accumulated process know-how that has proven notoriously hard to export.

companies.name: Samsung Foundry (Samsung Electronics)
companies.role: The world's second-largest contract foundry, and the only company that does both leading-edge logic and memory
companies.description: Samsung is the only firm on Earth running leading-edge logic foundry and leading-edge memory under one roof, and it was first to production with gate-all-around transistors at 3nm in 2022. Even so it holds under a tenth of the foundry market against TSMC's roughly two-thirds, because yield problems have repeatedly cost it flagship customers. Its EUV logic lines sit at Hwaseong (S3) and Pyeongtaek (S5) south of Seoul, and its $17bn+ Taylor, Texas fab is the US beachhead — Tesla's AI5 taped out on Samsung's 2nm node there in 2026, with ramp production due in 2027.

companies.name: Intel Corporation
companies.role: The one big fab that also designs its own chips, now selling foundry capacity to outside customers
companies.description: Intel is the odd one out among the four big fabs: it designs, manufactures and packages its own CPUs, and since 2021 has also been renting that manufacturing out to external customers as Intel Foundry. Its comeback bet is 18A, a 2nm-class node combining RibbonFET gate-all-around transistors with PowerVia backside power delivery, which entered production at Fab 52 on the Ocotillo campus in Chandler, Arizona at the end of 2025 — the first leading-edge node in years developed and ramped entirely on US soil. Process R&D still happens at D1X in Hillsboro, Oregon, the fab that decides what every other Intel site will build next.

companies.name: GlobalFoundries
companies.role: Foundry for the 'essential' chips — power, RF, automotive and industrial silicon on mature and specialty nodes
companies.description: Spun out of AMD's manufacturing arm in 2009, GlobalFoundries abandoned the leading-edge race in 2018 and now competes on specialty processes instead: 22FDX FD-SOI, RF-SOI for phone front-ends, power management and automotive-grade silicon. That sounds unglamorous until you notice it touches most of the chips in cars, base stations and satellites — the company reckons more than 60% of the market depends on the categories it serves. Fab 8 in Malta, New York is the largest leading-capability fab in the US at around 400,000 wafers a year, and Fab 1 in Dresden is the biggest chip plant in Europe, heading past one million wafers a year by 2028 under a €1.1bn expansion.

companies.name: SK hynix
companies.role: The world's leading maker of HBM — the stacked DRAM bolted onto every top-end AI accelerator
companies.description: SK hynix built its lead in high bandwidth memory by co-developing HBM with AMD a decade before anyone needed it, and it cashed in when the AI boom arrived: it was Nvidia's sole qualified HBM3 supplier, first to ship HBM3E in March 2024, and first to mass-produce 12-layer HBM3E in September 2024, holding an effective monopoly on Nvidia's top bins until Micron and Samsung qualified later. The whole AI data-centre build-out therefore rests on a memory stack designed in Icheon and assembled with TSV and bonding-wire processes that almost nobody outside South Korea can run at volume. Its Cheongju M15X fab is being tooled specifically as the company's HBM hub, and HBM output has been sold out a year or more in advance for several years running.

companies.name: Micron Technology
companies.role: The only US-headquartered DRAM maker, and the third source of HBM for AI accelerators
companies.description: Micron is the last American DRAM company and one of only three firms left that can make leading-edge DRAM at all. Its 30,000 m² mega campus on the outskirts of Taichung — across the road from rice farms — is its largest DRAM site and its main HBM packaging hub, running billions of dollars of lithography equipment around the clock. In December 2025 it announced it was shutting down its Crucial consumer brand entirely by February 2026, walking away from the home-PC market to redirect every available wafer to data-centre customers, which is about as blunt a signal of where the money is as an industry can send.

companies.name: Samsung Memory (Samsung Electronics)
companies.role: The world's largest maker of DRAM and NAND flash, and the third HBM supplier
companies.description: Samsung has been the number one memory maker since 1993 and holds roughly a third of the global DRAM market and a similar share of NAND, which means most phones, servers and SSDs on Earth contain its silicon. Its Pyeongtaek campus is the largest semiconductor manufacturing site in the world, big enough that each of its fab buildings dwarfs most companies' entire operations. In HBM it was the laggard — it spent well over a year failing Nvidia's qualification for HBM3E while SK hynix took the business — before finally clearing it, a rare case of the industry's biggest memory maker being locked out of its most profitable product.

companies.name: TSMC CoWoS (Advanced Packaging)
companies.role: The chip-on-wafer-on-substrate line that bonds GPU dies and HBM stacks onto a single silicon interposer
companies.description: CoWoS is the step that turns a GPU die and its ring of HBM stacks into one finished AI accelerator, mounting both on a silicon interposer and then onto a substrate. For roughly 18 months across 2024–25 this single process — concentrated almost entirely inside TSMC's own advanced packaging fabs in Taiwan — was the binding constraint on the entire AI industry: Nvidia could design all the chips it wanted and SK hynix could make all the memory it wanted, but nothing shipped faster than one packaging line in Taiwan could move. TSMC has been racing to catch up, roughly doubling capacity from about 35,000 wafers a month at the end of 2024 to around 75,000 a year later, with a target near 130,000 by late 2026 — and it is still reported as sold out.

companies.name: ASE Technology Holding
companies.role: The world's largest outsourced semiconductor assembly and test provider (OSAT)
companies.description: ASE is the biggest company in a business almost nobody outside the industry can name: taking finished wafers from foundries, dicing them, wiring or bumping the dies into packages, and testing the result before it ships. With around $18.5bn of revenue it is the largest OSAT on Earth by a wide margin — more than double its nearest rival — and together with subsidiary SPIL it handles a large slice of all outsourced packaging and test globally. Its home base is the Nanzih industrial park in Kaohsiung, and it has become the industry's designated overflow valve as AI demand outruns TSMC's in-house advanced packaging capacity, pouring billions into new FOCoS and 2.5D lines in Kaohsiung.

companies.name: Amkor Technology
companies.role: The world's second-largest OSAT and the main packaging partner for reshored US chip production
companies.description: Amkor essentially invented the outsourced packaging business in 1968 and is now the number two OSAT worldwide with roughly 15% of the market, running 2.5D/3D TSV, fan-out and flip-chip lines across Asia. Its strategic significance is geographic: a wafer finished at TSMC Arizona still had to fly to Taiwan to be packaged, which quietly undercut the whole point of reshoring. Amkor is fixing that with a $7bn advanced packaging and test campus in Peoria, Arizona — broken ground in October 2025, over 750,000 sq ft of cleanroom, production from early 2028 — built explicitly to finish TSMC's Arizona wafers on the same side of the Pacific, with Apple and Nvidia named as anchor customers.
